# Independent review of four frozen-model flags

Review date: October 18, 2026 (client date). Baseline: [0.32 report](../site/validation/student-models-032-2026-10-18.json), engine 3.4.0, created October 19 at 01:06 UTC (October 18 local). Answer-and-target hash: `9ca9ba4ca7af4b482fbbdad79a9d35b85dc8d936e9a25b43a2e712a702b607c6`.

I inspected the saved narrative, exact profession responses and result rows, and independently invoked the current engine for the four unchanged models. No fixture, target, engine, UI, build script or baseline output was modified. This is a synthetic behavioral review, not human predictive validation.

## Findings

| Case | Judgment | Evidence and generalizable response |
|---|---|---|
| `m32-salon-listener` | A real framing/eligibility issue; **not** an absence of all guidance. | Hairdresser has 8/8 task questions, all four refinements and several single-role option mappings, no field/route conflict. It is already rendered as a task lead. The sole missing task-supported criterion is the custom `r >= 0` gate: six-profile correlation is −.355. Calling this `no-clues` and telling the student “Your answers are still open” misdescribes highly specific choices. Show a primary task-contrast result with the actual preferred tasks and a separate broad-pattern disagreement; preserve the numerical correlation/official interpretation. Do not claim a high RIASEC match or measured dexterity. |
| `m32-food-without-sales` | A real false-precision issue in prominence; the alternative itself is plausible. | Food-counter, restaurant-cook and chef each receive the identical 8/8 task support, four refinements and the same four domain labels. Only counter work clears `r >= 0` (.076 vs cook −.284 and chef −.447), so it becomes the only featured role. The student chose preparing/timing food, not counter transactions or customers. The options currently do not distinguish those responsibilities adequately. Present an unresolved cooking/service comparison rather than a uniquely inferred counter role. Keep chef/head-cook leadership/experience requirements explicit: dislike of management means “chef” is not automatically the correct answer either. |
| `m32-biology-stories` | Mostly a sensible response-level disagreement; improve alternative visibility, not the target rank. | The student selected story through words/photos/moving images; scene revision; images/light/movement/sound **and** factual research; timing/movement/lighting refinement. These reasonably favor film-editing (8 task questions) over writing (7), which lacks the selected process/refinement item. Animation/photo also have 7. All four are internally `supported`; writing is not excluded as an unsuitable career. The three tied seven-question alternatives are omitted wholesale from featured results because one eight-question result plus that tier exceeds the three-card cap. Show their names together as related alternatives or offer an optional comparison. Do not feed narrative text to force writing, change its official answers, or claim writing was “wrongly rejected.” Preserve creative and science task pathways. |
| `m32-care-route-tension` | Substantively sensible conflict handling already; minor status taxonomy issue. | Physician has 10/10 task evidence, both specific responsibility selections and r=.900. The student explicitly chose dental-assisting preparation. Assisting has zero task evidence, not a hidden substitute career. The current UI already opens “Compare your preparation routes,” names physician work, states that the chosen route differs and links to comparison. Withholding an unqualified ready-to-follow physician route is sensible; recommending assisting from its shorter route alone would not be. Preserve this explicit comparison and truthful prerequisites. Internally, `preparation-conflict` would describe this better than `no-clues`. Expensive lifestyle goals should affect financial guidance, not medical interest scores. |

## General rule changes worth considering

1. **Separate evidence dimensions.** Keep official six-profile similarity, specific task interest, preparation conflicts and financial feasibility independently named. A custom task-contrast result can be useful even when the broad correlation is negative; it must not inherit a “strong O*NET match” label.
2. **Fix prominence and wording before changing cutoffs.** `no-clues` should not cover a strong task lead or explicit route conflict. A neutral “Work you want to explore” primary result can surface a strong specific lead with the disagreement visible. This avoids treating a mathematically tiny change around zero as a discontinuous change in personal suitability.
3. **Use discriminating evidence, not raw repetition alone.** Eight mapped prompts can repeat the same underlying interest. Most food selections map to three to five occupations; salon refinements are much more specific. Require evidence across real task/process/context distinctions and inspect mapping specificity before strengthening a task-based result. Do not call eight editorial questions eight independent validation observations.
4. **Preserve ambiguity without forced three cards.** If supported roles cannot be distinguished, show a compact named comparison group and an optional next experience. Do not choose a target by deterministic tie-breaking or add a mandatory survey merely to fill three slots.
5. **Use held-out contrasts when testing a general fix.** The same rule should retain explicit field dislikes, flat/all-positive responses, insufficient clinical responsibility detail and route conflicts. It should distinguish a kitchen-preparation interest from counter service only where actual answers provide that distinction. It should not promote every negative-correlation role indiscriminately.
